subject: Observability Integration: Dashboards, Traces & Alerting Runbook
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@cloudvista.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Observability Integration: Dashboards, Traces & Alerting Runbook

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the time today. As discussed on the call, we want to run a short implementation workshop to align on the observability handoff so your SREs can operate the service seamlessly after go-live. Proposed 30–45 minute agenda: 

- Quick inventory: list of services, DNS names, and current SLOs
- Dashboards: core widgets (latency P95/P99, request rate, error rate, token consumption) and baseline panels
- Tracing hooks: where to add span annotations for model calls, customer_id, prompt_id
- Error taxonomy: mapping CloudVista error codes to Redwood alert severities
- Alert routing & runbook: who owns each alert, escalation path, and PagerDuty mapping

Prior to the session it would help if you can share:
- Grafana access or screenshots of existing dashboards (read-only is fine)
- List of services + primary owners
- Any retention/KMS constraints for traces or logs

We can run the workshop next week — I’m available Tue/Wed 10–3 PT. If that works, I’ll invite the runbook owners from our side. Marissa and Ben are looped in to help draft the runbook and dashboard templates.

Attachments: none on this message (we'll share a starter runbook v1 after the workshop).

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Head of CS Ops, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
From: Alice Moreno <alice.moreno@cloudvista.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudVista Ops <ops@cloudvista.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Observability Integration: Dashboards, Traces & Alerting Runbook

Thanks Sean — Tue at 10:30 PT works for us. Quick answers to your pre-reqs: 

- Grafana: we can grant a read-only team account; I'll send an invite to ops@cloudvista.com and the redwood emails.
- Services: main entry points are api.cloudvista.com and ingestion.cloudvista.com; owners are Alice Moreno (api) and ops@cloudvista.com (ingestion).
- Retention/KMS: logs to our ELK are kept 90 days; traces to LightStep are 180 days. We have an HSM for encryption keys — if you need a key policy please let us know.

Also, can you include our security contact (security@cloudvista.com) on any artifact with an attached architecture diagram? They review all runbooks.

See you Tuesday 11/24 10:30 PT.

—Alice
Alice Moreno
Platform Engineering Manager, CloudVista
alice.moreno@cloudvista.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-20T10:28:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Observability Integration: Dashboards, Traces & Alerting Runbook

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Alice's responses. Action items for our side before the workshop: 

1) Marissa: draft a starter runbook that covers alert definitions, play-by-play for the most common incidents (high tail latency, model OOMs, auth errors), and an ownership matrix. Aim for a 1–2 page quick-run checklist plus a longer appendix.
2) Ben: assemble a dashboard template (Grafana JSON) with the panels we discussed; include sample queries and threshold recommendations.

Notes: CloudVista's retention windows: logs 90d, traces 180d — call out any KMS/HSM constraints. Also include a short section on how to instrument the model client for span context and prompt_id propagation.

I'll set the invite for 2026-11-24 10:30 PT and include security@cloudvista.com on the drive link.

Thanks — Sean

Date: 2026-11-23T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Observability Integration: Dashboards, Traces & Alerting Runbook — draft attached

Hi all —

Thanks for the details, Alice. Attached is a first-pass runbook (runbook-draft-v1.md) and a small bundle with example dashboard screenshots (dashboard-screenshots.zip). Highlights in the draft: 

- Incident playbooks (page 1): triage steps for high P99 latency, model OOMs, and authentication/permission failures.
- Error taxonomy (appendix A): mapping CloudVista error codes (CV-4xx, CV-5xx) to Redwood alert severities (info, warning, critical) and suggested PagerDuty escalation chains.
- Tracing guidance: client instrumentation snippet for propagating prompt_id, model_span_name, and customer_id; recommended span sampling rates to match your LightStep retention.
- Dashboard template: list of required panels and recommended thresholds; Grafana JSON will be uploaded to the shared drive after you confirm the structure.

Open items for the workshop:
- Confirm which CV-5xx codes are transient vs permanent for automatic retries.
- Agree on alert thresholds for reduced token throughput vs elevated latency.
- Decide on runbook ownership for the ingestion pipeline (CloudVista ops vs Redwood support during the 30-day ramp).

Link to doc: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-runbook-draft
Attachments: runbook-draft-v1.md (markdown), dashboard-screenshots.zip (3 PNGs, 1 JSON)

Please review and add comments directly in the Drive doc. I can incorporate feedback before Tuesday's workshop.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
